heading: Does one linear direction or persona feature mediate emergent misalignment across fine-tunes?
definition: one linear direction or persona feature mediates it across fine-tunes.
summary: Several groups find directions or persona features that carry over between some fine-tunes, but often only under certain conditions, or as model-specific sets of sparse-autoencoder features rather than one feature. In one study, directions from fine-tunes with different data formats did not converge, so a single shared mechanism is contested.

suggested_status.by_scale: Provisional pending the issue-9 study-level audit. 10-100B: C for an unrestricted shared-direction claim, with causal transfer under selected conditions. 1-10B: ? for the stated single-direction or single-feature claim; model-specific multi-latent interventions qualify its scope. Size not stated: R0 for the GPT-4o-specific persona-feature result.
suggested_status.reason: Medical-to-sports direction ablation supports partial cross-fine-tune mediation in Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct: the layer-24 medical-derived direction transfers across LoRA configurations and datasets, with coherence above 99% and norm-matched random-vector controls (arXiv:2506.11618#r7; arXiv:2506.11618#r8; arXiv:2506.11618#r9). BLOCK-EM instead establishes transfer of a finance-derived set of 20 layer-20 SAE latents across domains within Llama-3.1-8B (arXiv:2602.00767#R6; arXiv:2602.00767#R8). Llama-3.2-1B and Qwen2.5-7B use separately discovered model-specific sets, as specified in V5_checked.json.check_log for V5.support[4] and V5.against[2] (arXiv:2602.00767#R15; arXiv:2602.00767#R16). These results warrant limits_scope, not support for one shared direction or feature. Failed cross-format convergence in Olmo-3.1-32B and Qwen2.5-32B, and increased EM under code-donor direction ablation at layer 32 in the Olmo medical fine-tune, challenge unrestricted sharing (arXiv:2608.29118#R5; arXiv:2608.29118#R9; arXiv:2608.29118#R12). Own-direction ablation is excluded from cross-fine-tune evidence because it tests only within-fine-tune control (arXiv:2608.29118#R11). GPT-4o persona control across insecure-code and incorrect-advice fine-tunes uses steering selected to keep incoherence at or below 10%, and has multi-latent qualifications (arXiv:2506.19823#r21; arXiv:2506.19823#r22; arXiv:2506.19823#r23; arXiv:2506.19823#r24). The checked synthesis's scale coverage attributed to versions.V5.studies_by_size remains provisional pending the issue-9 audit; the cited rows establish the stated open-model sizes, while GPT-4o's size is unstated. The key versions.V5.studies_by_size comes from counts made before the checks and not rerun with their fixes; the studies index likewise still shows arXiv:2602.00767 as V5:S1L1, although the checked V5 synthesis and this status treat its V5 evidence as limits_scope. This reason quotes no V5 verdict tally, and none of the verdict, tranche or relation fixes the final critic named (for V1, V2, V4 and V6, and in the unfit check_log) concerns a study with a V5 verdict in the studies index, so the level does not rest on the stale tallies. Refreshed counts are needed before any V5 tally or size count is quoted. The supplied author metadata does not establish author independence; unmatched names and absent sharing markers do not resolve overlap. Review of the affected study-level audit entries remains unverified from the supplied materials. Corpus-wide check totals are not residual error estimates for this status.
suggested_status.open_questions: A matched replication transferring a fixed direction across advice and code fine-tunes, with random controls, coherent generation and preserved narrow capability, would clarify the contested scope. Cross-architecture transfer and comparison of single-direction with multi-feature interventions would determine whether the mechanism warrants a narrower claim.

source.title: Training large language models on narrow tasks can lead to broad misalignment
source.authors: Jan Betley; Daniel Tan; Niels Warncke; Anna Sztyber-Betley; Xuchan Bao; Mart'in Soto; Megha Srivastava; Nathan Labenz; Owain Evans

original_result.result: The original paper did not test this claim.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Emergent-misalignment LoRA adapters were far more alike in weight space than chess or safety-tuned control adapters.
Adding one difference-of-means direction induced emergent misalignment; removing that direction cut most of it across fine-tunes.
A toxic-persona sparse-autoencoder feature steered misalignment and separated misaligned from aligned models across GPT-4o fine-tunes.
Activation shifts along one 'evil' direction tracked how strongly two Qwen2.5-14B fine-tunes expressed that trait.
Blocking one fixed set of finance-derived sparse-autoencoder features cut emergent misalignment by about 93% across domains.
Adding or subtracting the sexual-advice direction in a risky-financial-advice model switched answers between harmful and benign.
Harm probes transferred above chance across all 30 Qwen 2.5 32B fine-tune pairs.
Restoring five selected attention heads to base-model outputs cut emergent misalignment; shared-head effects transferred between fine-tunes.
Fine-tunes trained on the same data format gave highly similar misalignment directions in Olmo and Qwen.
Projecting a frozen-model persona subspace out of activations during financial fine-tuning eliminated emergent misalignment.
Evil and semantic-valence vectors controlled Qwen-2.5 emergent misalignment, but the aligned base stayed near 0% misaligned.
Steering against an evil persona vector nearly eliminated emergent misalignment from GRPO on bad medical advice.
A transplanted code-fine-tune misalignment direction raised Qwen2.5-32B emergent misalignment above controls, but only to low rates.
Ablating ten persona features at one layer reduced misalignment in fine-tunes on bad medical advice.
Steering against persona vectors reversed trait shifts, and steering during training prevented them.
Steering against the global persona shift caused by fine-tuning lowered misalignment across Qwen models.
Emergent-misalignment adapters' weight updates overlapped only moderately, sharing a subspace rather than a single direction.
In Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a shared evil direction appeared only in contrastive weight vectors from opposite-behaviour fine-tunes.
The shared direction left some emergent misalignment unexplained, and its ablation transferred less well across datasets.
Steering ten sparse-autoencoder features gave different behaviour patterns; no fine-tune's pattern matched any single feature.
Suppressing emergent misalignment needed about 13 or more sparse-autoencoder features; longer training routed it around them.
Difference-of-means emergent-misalignment directions from different models overlapped weakly, with mean cosine similarity only 0.13–0.19.
Head replacement only modestly cut medical emergent misalignment; medical heads transferred only partly to other fine-tunes.
Ablating the single misalignment direction in a Qwen3-8B sycophancy fine-tune did not remove all emergent misalignment.
Inference-time ablation of the persona subspace removed only 36% of emergent misalignment; training-time removal cost capability.
In Llama-3.1-8B, amplifying the Evil and semantic-valence vectors barely changed emergent misalignment.
Steering on prompt and generated tokens left far more emergent misalignment than steering generated tokens only.
Ablating the medical fine-tune's own direction only halved its emergent misalignment; directions differed across training datasets.
Steering vectors from single-layer LoRAs only partly reproduced emergent misalignment, costing more coherence than the LoRAs.
Persona-feature ablation left residual misalignment, and the features also rose under benign fine-tuning.
Misalignment directions diverged across data formats; ablating a code fine-tune's direction in Olmo raised emergent misalignment.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Mediation by the same direction or persona feature across different model architectures.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V5.studies_by_family records family coverage, but not shared-vector transfer. arXiv:2608.11025#STEER-G3, arXiv:2608.11025#STEER-G2, arXiv:2608.11025#STEER-L31 and arXiv:2608.11025#STEER-Q25 use model-specific SAE features. arXiv:2607.04510#r16 tests base/instruct transplantation within Qwen2.5-32B. arXiv:2610.20887#R7 and arXiv:2610.20887#R20 concern shared head locations and transferred fixed-response head effects; directions are estimated separately for each organism, leaving mediation by one shared direction or persona feature untested.

untested.what: The shared-mechanism claim at toy scale, below 1B and above 100B.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V5.studies_by_size contains 1-10B, 10-100B and not stated, with no toy, <1B or >100B entry. Unstated proprietary-model sizes cannot establish coverage in those buckets.

untested.what: Transfer of one causal mediator across multiple RL fine-tunes, or between matched SFT and RL fine-tunes.
untested.basis: arXiv:2605.31328 Sections 5.1 and Appendix C.2 apply one extracted evil-persona vector to bad-medical GRPO mitigation configurations (arXiv:2605.31328#r44, arXiv:2605.31328#r45); Appendix D.7 tests inference-time steering on the unmitigated bad-medical GRPO model (arXiv:2605.31328#r50). No transfer test across multiple RL domains or matched SFT/RL fine-tunes is reported. counts: versions.V5.coverage_by_operation records interventions without a cross-training-route transfer category; arXiv:2506.19823#r21 and arXiv:2506.19823#r22 concern incorrect-advice and insecure-code fine-tunes.

wording_issues.phrase: one linear direction or persona feature
wording_issues.issue: BLOCK-EM transfers a set of 20 SAE latents across domains within Llama-3.1-8B; its other-model results use separately discovered model-specific sets. This is partial evidence for V5, without establishing mediation by one direction or feature. Other effective interventions include a rank-4 per-layer carrier, and GPT-4o fine-tune profiles do not match any single tested latent.

Transfer depends on dataset format and inducer. Cross-format direction ablation can increase EM, while whitened cross-inducer directions show limited overlap. Sharing demonstrated among selected advice fine-tunes does not establish sharing across arbitrary narrow datasets.
Weight similarity, activation projection and probe transfer establish association or shared geometry. They do not by themselves show that intervening on the measured direction changes EM.

In the Qwen2.5-14B extreme-sports model, medical-direction transfer ablation reduces EM by 78% relative to a pre-ablation EM rate of 20.2%, with coherence above 99%; suppression is partial. Other cited interventions also leave residual EM, and prevention can remove the narrow capability alongside EM. These results distinguish partial causal contribution from complete or capability-preserving mediation.

A global persona shift also appears in an aligned control, so the presence of that shift alone does not identify EM. Broad-misalignment steering-vector organisms in the same post are not fine-tuned organisms.
Some supporting interventions examine only a single fine-tuning domain or a single RL model; they show causal control without directly testing the across-fine-tune part.

method_sensitivity.what: Same-format advice/chat directions show strong similarity, while code-format directions can be nearly orthogonal. In Olmo medical EM, self-ablation at layer 32 reduces misaligned-and-coherent responses from 4.48% to 1.30%, while code-donor ablation increases EM. Self-ablation demonstrates control within one fine-tune; it does not establish mediation across fine-tunes.

Whitening substantially reduces apparent base–instruct persona alignment in Qwen2.5-32B. In Qwen2.5-7B weight space, contrastive vectors reveal small similarities among evil behavior vectors exceeding the control comparison, whereas raw task vectors do not group them. These are representation-dependent geometric associations, not tests of causal mediation across fine-tunes.

Applying a direction across residual-stream layers, at its source layer alone, or to an adapter B vector yields different EM reductions. In Qwen2.5-Coder, separately extracted directions from single-layer fine-tunes at layers 21, 31 and 41, applied at 150x, 35x and 20x respectively, partially reproduce misalignment with additional coherence loss. These separate-direction experiments leave shared mediation across fine-tunes untested.

Cross-domain steering at absolute coefficients of at least 7 produces qualitative coherence loss or collapse on one question, without reported post-steering EM rates. These observations provide method coverage, not a V5 verdict. GPT-4o persona steering is explicitly selected under an incoherence constraint, so its reported control applies within that selected operating range.

Evil/Semantic Valence Vector amplification strongly suppresses Qwen medical EM but has null or smaller effects in Llama. A separate global-persona-shift post reports successful steering across Qwen organisms and failed steering in Llama.
In preventive GRPO persona steering, decode-only intervention gives substantially lower residual EM than intervention on both prompt and decode tokens.

method_sensitivity.factor: Intervention timing and activation versus weight channel
method_sensitivity.what: Training-time activation hold-out prevents financial-organism EM while destroying narrow adherence. Post-training ablation only partially suppresses EM, and carrier projection from writer gradients is ineffective.

In BLOCK-EM's Llama-3.1-8B experiments, suppression strengthens with latent-set size, with a pronounced improvement around 13 latents. Latents 11–13 alone yield weak suppression. Re-emergence under longer training is consistent with rerouting around the blocked set. Cross-domain transfer of a finance-derived set of 20 SAE latents qualifies V5's single-direction wording; it does not establish mediation by one direction or feature.

Generated EM is measured after inference-time Base replacement of each organism's independently selected five heads. Cross-organism donor transfer instead uses three shared head locations and fixed-response preferences; zero-ablation diagnostics use the selected five heads and fixed-response preferences. Transfer recovery ratios do not establish equivalent effects during generation. These head-level experiments provide method coverage but leave mediation across fine-tunes by one shared direction or persona feature untested.

The data-attribution study uses separate SAE features for Gemma, Llama and Qwen, with model-specific steering strengths and a coherence constraint. These rows cover feature-based control across families but do not test transfer of one shared feature across models.

status_amendment.public_note: The summary now notes that this version's study counts were made before our error checks, and that our study index still gives one latent-blocking study a support verdict as well as a limit verdict, although we treat its evidence only as a limit on scope. The level (C) does not rest on those counts, so it is unchanged.
